  test-core:
    # Always runs (no job-level path gate): a path-filtered matrix skip
    # posts a check-run with the LITERAL unrendered name — the required
    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 12
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared changes — shard green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          name: coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

      # junit durations for the weekly shard-rebalance.yml (retention 7d so
      # a quiet week never starves it into the file-count fallback).

        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0

      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          name: coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

      # junit durations for the weekly shard-rebalance.yml (retention 7d so
      # a quiet week never starves it into the file-count fallback).

  test-core:
    # Always runs (no job-level path gate): a path-filtered matrix skip
    # posts a check-run with the LITERAL unrendered name — the required
    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 12
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared changes — shard green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0

        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          name: coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

      # junit durations for the weekly shard-rebalance.yml (retention 7d so
      # a quiet week never starves it into the file-count fallback).

          bash scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage "$next"
          # The staged tree must ANALYZE clean: v0.1.411 shipped files
          # with broken imports (the staging filter pruned lib/src/memory;
          # imports of fork-only dart_tui symbols) that only a consumer's
          # `dart analyze` ever surfaced (issue #613). Errors fail the
          # gate; warnings/infos pass, matching the static analyze stage.
          (cd /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage && dart pub get && dart analyze)
          (cd /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage && dart pub publish --dry-run --ignore-warnings)

  test-core:
    # Always runs (no job-level path gate): a path-filtered matrix skip
    # posts a check-run with the LITERAL unrendered name — the required
    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 12
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared changes — shard green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})

  test-core:
    # Always runs (no job-level path gate): a path-filtered matrix skip
    # posts a check-run with the LITERAL unrendered name — the required
    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 12
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared changes — shard green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          name: coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

      # junit durations for the weekly shard-rebalance.yml (retention 7d so
      # a quiet week never starves it into the file-count fallback).

content.text:
# Issue #194 (point 4): per-step duration telemetry. The jobs API already
  # records started/completed per step — dump it as a summary table plus a
  # raw artifact instead of instrumenting every step by hand.
  step-timings:
    name: Per-step timing telemetry
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      actions: read
    steps:
      - name: Collect per-step durations
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The jobs endpoint intermittently answers 502 (live on the
          # gh-1086 rework head 81ed7186: a single 502 failed the whole
          # telemetry leg). Same 3-attempt pattern as build-mobile's
          # "Install Flutter dependencies" — transient API errors retry,
          # a real failure still reds the step loudly.
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" > /tmp/jobs.json; then
              break
            fi
            if [ "$attempt" = 3 ]; then
              echo "::error::gh api jobs fetch failed after 3 attempts — GitHub API is erroring (502-class)"
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "::warning::gh api jobs fetch failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
            sleep 10
          done
          python3 - <<'EOF' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          import datetime, json
          jobs = json.load(open('/tmp/jobs.json'))['jobs']
          print('## Per-step durations\n')
          print('| job | step | duration | conclusion |')
          print('|---|---|---|---|')
          for j in jobs:
              for s in j.get('steps', []):
                  if not (s.get('started_at') and s.get('completed_at')):
                      continue
                  t0 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['started_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  t1 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['completed_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  print(f"| {j['name']} | {s['name']} | {int((t1 - t0).total_seconds())}s | {s['conclusion']} |")
          EOF
          cp /tmp/jobs.json step-timings.json

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: step-timings
          path: step-timings.json
          retention-days: 14

  # Issue #194 (point 4): >2x-baseline watchdog. The timeout-minutes above
  # are ≈2x the healthy job durations observed on main (shards 3-5 min,
  # flutter-tests ~6 min + fa_ui shards ~5 min since issue #283). A timeout means this run landed on a degraded
  # runner allocation; the remedy is a fresh EMPTY-COMMIT push — a new run
  # gets a fresh allocation and the push cancels this stale run via the PR
  # concurrency group. NEVER `gh run rerun`: it reallocates into the same
  # degraded pool. One retrigger max per head commit (loop guard below).
  watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # empty-commit retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs only: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref.
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Detect a timeout-type failure
        id: trip
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          trip=false
          for id in $(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '.jobs[] | select(.conclusion=="failure") | .id'); do
            # A job-level timeout cancels the running step: the job is
            # 'failure' but its LAST step is 'cancelled'. A real test
            # failure ends with a failed step.

# Issue #194 (point 4): per-step duration telemetry. The jobs API already
  # records started/completed per step — dump it as a summary table plus a
  # raw artifact instead of instrumenting every step by hand.
  step-timings:
    name: Per-step timing telemetry
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      actions: read
    steps:
      - name: Collect per-step durations
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The jobs endpoint intermittently answers 502 (live on the
          # gh-1086 rework head 81ed7186: a single 502 failed the whole
          # telemetry leg). Same 3-attempt pattern as build-mobile's
          # "Install Flutter dependencies" — transient API errors retry,
          # a real failure still reds the step loudly.
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" > /tmp/jobs.json; then
              break
            fi
            if [ "$attempt" = 3 ]; then
              echo "::error::gh api jobs fetch failed after 3 attempts — GitHub API is erroring (502-class)"
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "::warning::gh api jobs fetch failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
            sleep 10
          done
          python3 - <<'EOF' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          import datetime, json
          jobs = json.load(open('/tmp/jobs.json'))['jobs']
          print('## Per-step durations\n')
          print('| job | step | duration | conclusion |')
          print('|---|---|---|---|')
          for j in jobs:
              for s in j.get('steps', []):
                  if not (s.get('started_at') and s.get('completed_at')):
                      continue
                  t0 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['started_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  t1 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['completed_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  print(f"| {j['name']} | {s['name']} | {int((t1 - t0).total_seconds())}s | {s['conclusion']} |")
          EOF
          cp /tmp/jobs.json step-timings.json

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: step-timings
          path: step-timings.json
          retention-days: 14

  # Issue #194 (point 4): >2x-baseline watchdog. The timeout-minutes above
  # are ≈2x the healthy job durations observed on main (shards 3-5 min,
  # flutter-tests ~6 min + fa_ui shards ~5 min since issue #283). A timeout means this run landed on a degraded
  # runner allocation; the remedy is a fresh EMPTY-COMMIT push — a new run
  # gets a fresh allocation and the push cancels this stale run via the PR
  # concurrency group. NEVER `gh run rerun`: it reallocates into the same
  # degraded pool. One retrigger max per head commit (loop guard below).
  watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # empty-commit retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs only: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref.
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Detect a timeout-type failure
        id: trip
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          trip=false
          for id in $(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '.jobs[] | select(.conclusion=="failure") | .id'); do
            # A job-level timeout cancels the running step: the job is
            # 'failure' but its LAST step is 'cancelled'. A real test

blocks.text:
# Issue #194 (point 4): per-step duration telemetry. The jobs API already
  # records started/completed per step — dump it as a summary table plus a
  # raw artifact instead of instrumenting every step by hand.
  step-timings:
    name: Per-step timing telemetry
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      actions: read
    steps:
      - name: Collect per-step durations
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The jobs endpoint intermittently answers 502 (live on the
          # gh-1086 rework head 81ed7186: a single 502 failed the whole
          # telemetry leg). Same 3-attempt pattern as build-mobile's
          # "Install Flutter dependencies" — transient API errors retry,
          # a real failure still reds the step loudly.
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" > /tmp/jobs.json; then
              break
            fi
            if [ "$attempt" = 3 ]; then
              echo "::error::gh api jobs fetch failed after 3 attempts — GitHub API is erroring (502-class)"
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "::warning::gh api jobs fetch failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
            sleep 10
          done
          python3 - <<'EOF' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          import datetime, json
          jobs = json.load(open('/tmp/jobs.json'))['jobs']
          print('## Per-step durations\n')
          print('| job | step | duration | conclusion |')
          print('|---|---|---|---|')
          for j in jobs:
              for s in j.get('steps', []):
                  if not (s.get('started_at') and s.get('completed_at')):
                      continue
                  t0 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['started_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  t1 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['completed_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  print(f"| {j['name']} | {s['name']} | {int((t1 - t0).total_seconds())}s | {s['conclusion']} |")
          EOF
          cp /tmp/jobs.json step-timings.json

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: step-timings
          path: step-timings.json
          retention-days: 14

  # Issue #194 (point 4): >2x-baseline watchdog. The timeout-minutes above
  # are ≈2x the healthy job durations observed on main (shards 3-5 min,
  # flutter-tests ~6 min + fa_ui shards ~5 min since issue #283). A timeout means this run landed on a degraded
  # runner allocation; the remedy is a fresh EMPTY-COMMIT push — a new run
  # gets a fresh allocation and the push cancels this stale run via the PR
  # concurrency group. NEVER `gh run rerun`: it reallocates into the same
  # degraded pool. One retrigger max per head commit (loop guard below).
  watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # empty-commit retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs only: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref.
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Detect a timeout-type failure
        id: trip
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          trip=false
          for id in $(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '.jobs[] | select(.conclusion=="failure") | .id'); do
            # A job-level timeout cancels the running step: the job is
            # 'failure' but its LAST step is 'cancelled'. A real test
            # failure ends with a failed step.

blocks.text:
# Issue #194 (point 4): per-step duration telemetry. The jobs API already
  # records started/completed per step — dump it as a summary table plus a
  # raw artifact instead of instrumenting every step by hand.
  step-timings:
    name: Per-step timing telemetry
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      actions: read
    steps:
      - name: Collect per-step durations
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The jobs endpoint intermittently answers 502 (live on the
          # gh-1086 rework head 81ed7186: a single 502 failed the whole
          # telemetry leg). Same 3-attempt pattern as build-mobile's
          # "Install Flutter dependencies" — transient API errors retry,
          # a real failure still reds the step loudly.
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" > /tmp/jobs.json; then
              break
            fi
            if [ "$attempt" = 3 ]; then
              echo "::error::gh api jobs fetch failed after 3 attempts — GitHub API is erroring (502-class)"
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "::warning::gh api jobs fetch failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
            sleep 10
          done
          python3 - <<'EOF' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          import datetime, json
          jobs = json.load(open('/tmp/jobs.json'))['jobs']
          print('## Per-step durations\n')
          print('| job | step | duration | conclusion |')
          print('|---|---|---|---|')
          for j in jobs:
              for s in j.get('steps', []):
                  if not (s.get('started_at') and s.get('completed_at')):
                      continue
                  t0 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['started_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  t1 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['completed_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  print(f"| {j['name']} | {s['name']} | {int((t1 - t0).total_seconds())}s | {s['conclusion']} |")
          EOF
          cp /tmp/jobs.json step-timings.json

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: step-timings
          path: step-timings.json
          retention-days: 14

  # Issue #194 (point 4): >2x-baseline watchdog. The timeout-minutes above
  # are ≈2x the healthy job durations observed on main (shards 3-5 min,
  # flutter-tests ~6 min + fa_ui shards ~5 min since issue #283). A timeout means this run landed on a degraded
  # runner allocation; the remedy is a fresh EMPTY-COMMIT push — a new run
  # gets a fresh allocation and the push cancels this stale run via the PR
  # concurrency group. NEVER `gh run rerun`: it reallocates into the same
  # degraded pool. One retrigger max per head commit (loop guard below).
  watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # empty-commit retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs only: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref.
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Detect a timeout-type failure
        id: trip
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          trip=false
          for id in $(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '.jobs[] | select(.conclusion=="failure") | .id'); do
            # A job-level timeout cancels the running step: the job is
            # 'failure' but its LAST step is 'cancelled'. A real test
            # failure ends with a failed step.

blocks.text:
# Issue #194 (point 4): per-step duration telemetry. The jobs API already
  # records started/completed per step — dump it as a summary table plus a
  # raw artifact instead of instrumenting every step by hand.
  step-timings:
    name: Per-step timing telemetry
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      actions: read
    steps:
      - name: Collect per-step durations
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The jobs endpoint intermittently answers 502 (live on the
          # gh-1086 rework head 81ed7186: a single 502 failed the whole
          # telemetry leg). Same 3-attempt pattern as build-mobile's
          # "Install Flutter dependencies" — transient API errors retry,
          # a real failure still reds the step loudly.
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" > /tmp/jobs.json; then
              break
            fi
            if [ "$attempt" = 3 ]; then
              echo "::error::gh api jobs fetch failed after 3 attempts — GitHub API is erroring (502-class)"
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "::warning::gh api jobs fetch failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
            sleep 10
          done
          python3 - <<'EOF' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          import datetime, json
          jobs = json.load(open('/tmp/jobs.json'))['jobs']
          print('## Per-step durations\n')
          print('| job | step | duration | conclusion |')
          print('|---|---|---|---|')
          for j in jobs:
              for s in j.get('steps', []):
                  if not (s.get('started_at') and s.get('completed_at')):
                      continue
                  t0 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['started_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  t1 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['completed_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  print(f"| {j['name']} | {s['name']} | {int((t1 - t0).total_seconds())}s | {s['conclusion']} |")
          EOF
          cp /tmp/jobs.json step-timings.json

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: step-timings
          path: step-timings.json
          retention-days: 14

  # Issue #194 (point 4): >2x-baseline watchdog. The timeout-minutes above
  # are ≈2x the healthy job durations observed on main (shards 3-5 min,
  # flutter-tests ~6 min + fa_ui shards ~5 min since issue #283). A timeout means this run landed on a degraded
  # runner allocation; the remedy is a fresh EMPTY-COMMIT push — a new run
  # gets a fresh allocation and the push cancels this stale run via the PR
  # concurrency group. NEVER `gh run rerun`: it reallocates into the same
  # degraded pool. One retrigger max per head commit (loop guard below).
  watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # empty-commit retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs only: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref.
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Detect a timeout-type failure
        id: trip
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          trip=false
          for id in $(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '.jobs[] | select(.conclusion=="failure") | .id'); do
            # A job-level timeout cancels the running step: the job is
            # 'failure' but its LAST step is 'cancelled'. A real test
            # failure ends with a failed step.

blocks.text:
# Issue #194 (point 4): per-step duration telemetry. The jobs API already
  # records started/completed per step — dump it as a summary table plus a
  # raw artifact instead of instrumenting every step by hand.
  step-timings:
    name: Per-step timing telemetry
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      actions: read
    steps:
      - name: Collect per-step durations
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The jobs endpoint intermittently answers 502 (live on the
          # gh-1086 rework head 81ed7186: a single 502 failed the whole
          # telemetry leg). Same 3-attempt pattern as build-mobile's
          # "Install Flutter dependencies" — transient API errors retry,
          # a real failure still reds the step loudly.
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" > /tmp/jobs.json; then
              break
            fi
            if [ "$attempt" = 3 ]; then
              echo "::error::gh api jobs fetch failed after 3 attempts — GitHub API is erroring (502-class)"
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "::warning::gh api jobs fetch failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
            sleep 10
          done
          python3 - <<'EOF' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          import datetime, json
          jobs = json.load(open('/tmp/jobs.json'))['jobs']
          print('## Per-step durations\n')
          print('| job | step | duration | conclusion |')
          print('|---|---|---|---|')
          for j in jobs:
              for s in j.get('steps', []):
                  if not (s.get('started_at') and s.get('completed_at')):
                      continue
                  t0 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['started_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  t1 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['completed_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  print(f"| {j['name']} | {s['name']} | {int((t1 - t0).total_seconds())}s | {s['conclusion']} |")
          EOF
          cp /tmp/jobs.json step-timings.json

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: step-timings
          path: step-timings.json
          retention-days: 14

  # Issue #194 (point 4): >2x-baseline watchdog. The timeout-minutes above
  # are ≈2x the healthy job durations observed on main (shards 3-5 min,
  # flutter-tests ~6 min + fa_ui shards ~5 min since issue #283). A timeout means this run landed on a degraded
  # runner allocation; the remedy is a fresh EMPTY-COMMIT push — a new run
  # gets a fresh allocation and the push cancels this stale run via the PR
  # concurrency group. NEVER `gh run rerun`: it reallocates into the same
  # degraded pool. One retrigger max per head commit (loop guard below).
  watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # empty-commit retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs only: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref.
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Detect a timeout-type failure
        id: trip
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          trip=false
          for id in $(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '.jobs[] | select(.conclusion=="failure") | .id'); do
            # A job-level timeout cancels the running step: the job is
            # 'failure' but its LAST step is 'cancelled'. A real test
            # failure ends with a failed step.

# Issue #194 (point 4): per-step duration telemetry. The jobs API already
  # records started/completed per step — dump it as a summary table plus a

blocks.text:
# Issue #194 (point 4): per-step duration telemetry. The jobs API already
  # records started/completed per step — dump it as a summary table plus a
  # raw artifact instead of instrumenting every step by hand.
  step-timings:
    name: Per-step timing telemetry
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      actions: read
    steps:
      - name: Collect per-step durations
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The jobs endpoint intermittently answers 502 (live on the
          # gh-1086 rework head 81ed7186: a single 502 failed the whole
          # telemetry leg). Same 3-attempt pattern as build-mobile's
          # "Install Flutter dependencies" — transient API errors retry,
          # a real failure still reds the step loudly.
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" > /tmp/jobs.json; then
              break
            fi
            if [ "$attempt" = 3 ]; then
              echo "::error::gh api jobs fetch failed after 3 attempts — GitHub API is erroring (502-class)"
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "::warning::gh api jobs fetch failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
            sleep 10
          done
          python3 - <<'EOF' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          import datetime, json
          jobs = json.load(open('/tmp/jobs.json'))['jobs']
          print('## Per-step durations\n')
          print('| job | step | duration | conclusion |')
          print('|---|---|---|---|')
          for j in jobs:
              for s in j.get('steps', []):
                  if not (s.get('started_at') and s.get('completed_at')):
                      continue
                  t0 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['started_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  t1 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['completed_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  print(f"| {j['name']} | {s['name']} | {int((t1 - t0).total_seconds())}s | {s['conclusion']} |")
          EOF
          cp /tmp/jobs.json step-timings.json

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: step-timings
          path: step-timings.json
          retention-days: 14

  # Issue #194 (point 4): >2x-baseline watchdog. The timeout-minutes above
  # are ≈2x the healthy job durations observed on main (shards 3-5 min,
  # flutter-tests ~6 min + fa_ui shards ~5 min since issue #283). A timeout means this run landed on a degraded
  # runner allocation; the remedy is a fresh EMPTY-COMMIT push — a new run
  # gets a fresh allocation and the push cancels this stale run via the PR
  # concurrency group. NEVER `gh run rerun`: it reallocates into the same
  # degraded pool. One retrigger max per head commit (loop guard below).
  watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # empty-commit retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs only: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref.
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Detect a timeout-type failure
        id: trip
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          trip=false
          for id in $(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '.jobs[] | select(.conclusion=="failure") | .id'); do
            # A job-level timeout cancels the running step: the job is
            # 'failure' but its LAST step is 'cancelled'. A real test
            # failure ends with a failed step.

blocks.text:
# Issue #194 (point 4): per-step duration telemetry. The jobs API already
  # records started/completed per step — dump it as a summary table plus a
  # raw artifact instead of instrumenting every step by hand.
  step-timings:
    name: Per-step timing telemetry
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      actions: read
    steps:
      - name: Collect per-step durations
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The jobs endpoint intermittently answers 502 (live on the
          # gh-1086 rework head 81ed7186: a single 502 failed the whole
          # telemetry leg). Same 3-attempt pattern as build-mobile's
          # "Install Flutter dependencies" — transient API errors retry,
          # a real failure still reds the step loudly.
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" > /tmp/jobs.json; then
              break
            fi
            if [ "$attempt" = 3 ]; then
              echo "::error::gh api jobs fetch failed after 3 attempts — GitHub API is erroring (502-class)"
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "::warning::gh api jobs fetch failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
            sleep 10
          done
          python3 - <<'EOF' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          import datetime, json
          jobs = json.load(open('/tmp/jobs.json'))['jobs']
          print('## Per-step durations\n')
          print('| job | step | duration | conclusion |')
          print('|---|---|---|---|')
          for j in jobs:
              for s in j.get('steps', []):
                  if not (s.get('started_at') and s.get('completed_at')):
                      continue
                  t0 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['started_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  t1 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['completed_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  print(f"| {j['name']} | {s['name']} | {int((t1 - t0).total_seconds())}s | {s['conclusion']} |")
          EOF
          cp /tmp/jobs.json step-timings.json

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: step-timings
          path: step-timings.json
          retention-days: 14

  # Issue #194 (point 4): >2x-baseline watchdog. The timeout-minutes above
  # are ≈2x the healthy job durations observed on main (shards 3-5 min,
  # flutter-tests ~6 min + fa_ui shards ~5 min since issue #283). A timeout means this run landed on a degraded
  # runner allocation; the remedy is a fresh EMPTY-COMMIT push — a new run
  # gets a fresh allocation and the push cancels this stale run via the PR
  # concurrency group. NEVER `gh run rerun`: it reallocates into the same
  # degraded pool. One retrigger max per head commit (loop guard below).
  watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # empty-commit retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs only: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref.
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Detect a timeout-type failure
        id: trip
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          trip=false
          for id in $(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '.jobs[] | select(.conclusion=="failure") | .id'); do
            # A job-level timeout cancels the running step: the job is
            # 'failure' but its LAST step is 'cancelled'. A real test
            # failure ends with a failed step.

blocks.text:
# Issue #194 (point 4): per-step duration telemetry. The jobs API already
  # records started/completed per step — dump it as a summary table plus a
  # raw artifact instead of instrumenting every step by hand.
  step-timings:
    name: Per-step timing telemetry
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      actions: read
    steps:
      - name: Collect per-step durations
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The jobs endpoint intermittently answers 502 (live on the
          # gh-1086 rework head 81ed7186: a single 502 failed the whole
          # telemetry leg). Same 3-attempt pattern as build-mobile's
          # "Install Flutter dependencies" — transient API errors retry,
          # a real failure still reds the step loudly.
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" > /tmp/jobs.json; then
              break
            fi
            if [ "$attempt" = 3 ]; then
              echo "::error::gh api jobs fetch failed after 3 attempts — GitHub API is erroring (502-class)"
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "::warning::gh api jobs fetch failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
            sleep 10
          done
          python3 - <<'EOF' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          import datetime, json
          jobs = json.load(open('/tmp/jobs.json'))['jobs']
          print('## Per-step durations\n')
          print('| job | step | duration | conclusion |')
          print('|---|---|---|---|')
          for j in jobs:
              for s in j.get('steps', []):
                  if not (s.get('started_at') and s.get('completed_at')):
                      continue
                  t0 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['started_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  t1 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['completed_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  print(f"| {j['name']} | {s['name']} | {int((t1 - t0).total_seconds())}s | {s['conclusion']} |")
          EOF
          cp /tmp/jobs.json step-timings.json

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: step-timings
          path: step-timings.json
          retention-days: 14

  # Issue #194 (point 4): >2x-baseline watchdog. The timeout-minutes above
  # are ≈2x the healthy job durations observed on main (shards 3-5 min,
  # flutter-tests ~6 min + fa_ui shards ~5 min since issue #283). A timeout means this run landed on a degraded
  # runner allocation; the remedy is a fresh EMPTY-COMMIT push — a new run
  # gets a fresh allocation and the push cancels this stale run via the PR
  # concurrency group. NEVER `gh run rerun`: it reallocates into the same
  # degraded pool. One retrigger max per head commit (loop guard below).
  watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # empty-commit retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs only: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref.
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Detect a timeout-type failure
        id: trip
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          trip=false
          for id in $(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '.jobs[] | select(.conclusion=="failure") | .id'); do
            # A job-level timeout cancels the running step: the job is
            # 'failure' but its LAST step is 'cancelled'. A real test
            # failure ends with a failed step.

# Issue #194 (point 4): per-step duration telemetry. The jobs API already
  # records started/completed per step — dump it as a summary table plus a
  # raw artifact instead of instrumenting every step by hand.
  step-timings:
    name: Per-step timing telemetry
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      actions: read
    steps:
      - name: Collect per-step durations
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The jobs endpoint intermittently answers 502 (live on the
          # gh-1086 rework head 81ed7186: a single 502 failed the whole
          # telemetry leg). Same 3-attempt pattern as build-mobile's
          # "Install Flutter dependencies" — transient API errors retry,
          # a real failure still reds the step loudly.
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" > /tmp/jobs.json; then
              break
            fi
            if [ "$attempt" = 3 ]; then
              echo "::error::gh api jobs fetch failed after 3 attempts — GitHub API is erroring (502-class)"
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "::warning::gh api jobs fetch failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
            sleep 10
          done
          python3 - <<'EOF' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          import datetime, json
          jobs = json.load(open('/tmp/jobs.json'))['jobs']
          print('## Per-step durations\n')
          print('| job | step | duration | conclusion |')

# Issue #194 (point 4): per-step duration telemetry. The jobs API already
  # records started/completed per step — dump it as a summary table plus a
  # raw artifact instead of instrumenting every step by hand.
  step-timings:
    name: Per-step timing telemetry
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      actions: read
    steps:
      - name: Collect per-step durations
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The jobs endpoint intermittently answers 502 (live on the
          # gh-1086 rework head 81ed7186: a single 502 failed the whole
          # telemetry leg). Same 3-attempt pattern as build-mobile's
          # "Install Flutter dependencies" — transient API errors retry,
          # a real failure still reds the step loudly.
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" > /tmp/jobs.json; then
              break
            fi
            if [ "$attempt" = 3 ]; then
              echo "::error::gh api jobs fetch failed after 3 attempts — GitHub API is erroring (502-class)"
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "::warning::gh api jobs fetch failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
            sleep 10
          done
          python3 - <<'EOF' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          import datetime, json
          jobs = json.load(open('/tmp/jobs.json'))['jobs']
          print('## Per-step durations\n')
          print('| job | step | duration | conclusion |')
          print('|---|---|---|---|')
          for j in jobs:
              for s in j.get('steps', []):
                  if not (s.get('started_at') and s.get('completed_at')):
                      continue
                  t0 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['started_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  t1 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['completed_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  print(f"| {j['name']} | {s['name']} | {int((t1 - t0).total_seconds())}s | {s['conclusion']} |")
          EOF
          cp /tmp/jobs.json step-timings.json

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: step-timings
          path: step-timings.json
          retention-days: 14

  # Issue #194 (point 4): >2x-baseline watchdog. The timeout-minutes above
  # are ≈2x the healthy job durations observed on main (shards 3-5 min,
  # flutter-tests ~6 min + fa_ui shards ~5 min since issue #283). A timeout means this run landed on a degraded
  # runner allocation; the remedy is a fresh EMPTY-COMMIT push — a new run
  # gets a fresh allocation and the push cancels this stale run via the PR
  # concurrency group. NEVER `gh run rerun`: it reallocates into the same
  # degraded pool. One retrigger max per head commit (loop guard below).
  watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # empty-commit retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs only: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref.
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Detect a timeout-type failure
        id: trip
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          trip=false
          for id in $(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '.jobs[] | select(.conclusion=="failure") | .id'); do
            # A job-level timeout cancels the running step: the job is
            # 'failure' but its LAST step is 'cancelled'. A real test
            # failure ends with a failed step.

blocks.text:
# Issue #194 (point 4): per-step duration telemetry. The jobs API already
  # records started/completed per step — dump it as a summary table plus a
  # raw artifact instead of instrumenting every step by hand.
  step-timings:
    name: Per-step timing telemetry
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      actions: read
    steps:
      - name: Collect per-step durations
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The jobs endpoint intermittently answers 502 (live on the
          # gh-1086 rework head 81ed7186: a single 502 failed the whole
          # telemetry leg). Same 3-attempt pattern as build-mobile's
          # "Install Flutter dependencies" — transient API errors retry,
          # a real failure still reds the step loudly.
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" > /tmp/jobs.json; then
              break
            fi
            if [ "$attempt" = 3 ]; then
              echo "::error::gh api jobs fetch failed after 3 attempts — GitHub API is erroring (502-class)"
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "::warning::gh api jobs fetch failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
            sleep 10
          done
          python3 - <<'EOF' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          import datetime, json
          jobs = json.load(open('/tmp/jobs.json'))['jobs']
          print('## Per-step durations\n')
          print('| job | step | duration | conclusion |')
          print('|---|---|---|---|')
          for j in jobs:
              for s in j.get('steps', []):
                  if not (s.get('started_at') and s.get('completed_at')):
                      continue
                  t0 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['started_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  t1 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['completed_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  print(f"| {j['name']} | {s['name']} | {int((t1 - t0).total_seconds())}s | {s['conclusion']} |")
          EOF
          cp /tmp/jobs.json step-timings.json

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: step-timings
          path: step-timings.json
          retention-days: 14

  # Issue #194 (point 4): >2x-baseline watchdog. The timeout-minutes above
  # are ≈2x the healthy job durations observed on main (shards 3-5 min,
  # flutter-tests ~6 min + fa_ui shards ~5 min since issue #283). A timeout means this run landed on a degraded
  # runner allocation; the remedy is a fresh EMPTY-COMMIT push — a new run
  # gets a fresh allocation and the push cancels this stale run via the PR
  # concurrency group. NEVER `gh run rerun`: it reallocates into the same
  # degraded pool. One retrigger max per head commit (loop guard below).
  watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # empty-commit retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs only: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref.
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Detect a timeout-type failure
        id: trip
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          trip=false
          for id in $(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '.jobs[] | select(.conclusion=="failure") | .id'); do
            # A job-level timeout cancels the running step: the job is
            # 'failure' but its LAST step is 'cancelled'. A real test
            # failure ends with a failed step.
