blocks.text:
# Issue #194 (point 4): per-step duration telemetry. The jobs API already
  # records started/completed per step — dump it as a summary table plus a
  # raw artifact instead of instrumenting every step by hand.
  step-timings:
    name: Per-step timing telemetry
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      actions: read
    steps:
      - name: Collect per-step durations
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The jobs endpoint intermittently answers 502 (live on the
          # gh-1086 rework head 81ed7186: a single 502 failed the whole
          # telemetry leg). Same 3-attempt pattern as build-mobile's
          # "Install Flutter dependencies" — transient API errors retry,
          # a real failure still reds the step loudly.
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" > /tmp/jobs.json; then
              break
            fi
            if [ "$attempt" = 3 ]; then
              echo "::error::gh api jobs fetch failed after 3 attempts — GitHub API is erroring (502-class)"
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "::warning::gh api jobs fetch failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
            sleep 10
          done
          python3 - <<'EOF' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          import datetime, json
          jobs = json.load(open('/tmp/jobs.json'))['jobs']
          print('## Per-step durations\n')
          print('| job | step | duration | conclusion |')
          print('|---|---|---|---|')
          for j in jobs:
              for s in j.get('steps', []):
                  if not (s.get('started_at') and s.get('completed_at')):
                      continue
                  t0 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['started_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  t1 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['completed_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  print(f"| {j['name']} | {s['name']} | {int((t1 - t0).total_seconds())}s | {s['conclusion']} |")
          EOF
          cp /tmp/jobs.json step-timings.json

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: step-timings
          path: step-timings.json
          retention-days: 14

  # Issue #194 (point 4): >2x-baseline watchdog. The timeout-minutes above
  # are ≈2x the healthy job durations observed on main (shards 3-5 min,
  # flutter-tests ~6 min + fa_ui shards ~5 min since issue #283). A timeout means this run landed on a degraded
  # runner allocation; the remedy is a fresh EMPTY-COMMIT push — a new run
  # gets a fresh allocation and the push cancels this stale run via the PR
  # concurrency group. NEVER `gh run rerun`: it reallocates into the same
  # degraded pool. One retrigger max per head commit (loop guard below).
  watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # empty-commit retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs only: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref.
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Detect a timeout-type failure
        id: trip
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}

blocks.text:
# Issue #194 (point 4): per-step duration telemetry. The jobs API already
  # records started/completed per step — dump it as a summary table plus a
  # raw artifact instead of instrumenting every step by hand.
  step-timings:
    name: Per-step timing telemetry
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      actions: read
    steps:
      - name: Collect per-step durations
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The jobs endpoint intermittently answers 502 (live on the
          # gh-1086 rework head 81ed7186: a single 502 failed the whole
          # telemetry leg). Same 3-attempt pattern as build-mobile's
          # "Install Flutter dependencies" — transient API errors retry,
          # a real failure still reds the step loudly.
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" > /tmp/jobs.json; then
              break
            fi
            if [ "$attempt" = 3 ]; then
              echo "::error::gh api jobs fetch failed after 3 attempts — GitHub API is erroring (502-class)"
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "::warning::gh api jobs fetch failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
            sleep 10
          done
          python3 - <<'EOF' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          import datetime, json
          jobs = json.load(open('/tmp/jobs.json'))['jobs']
          print('## Per-step durations\n')
          print('| job | step | duration | conclusion |')
          print('|---|---|---|---|')
          for j in jobs:
              for s in j.get('steps', []):
                  if not (s.get('started_at') and s.get('completed_at')):
                      continue
                  t0 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['started_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  t1 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['completed_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  print(f"| {j['name']} | {s['name']} | {int((t1 - t0).total_seconds())}s | {s['conclusion']} |")
          EOF
          cp /tmp/jobs.json step-timings.json

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: step-timings
          path: step-timings.json
          retention-days: 14

  # Issue #194 (point 4): >2x-baseline watchdog. The timeout-minutes above
  # are ≈2x the healthy job durations observed on main (shards 3-5 min,
  # flutter-tests ~6 min + fa_ui shards ~5 min since issue #283). A timeout means this run landed on a degraded
  # runner allocation; the remedy is a fresh EMPTY-COMMIT push — a new run
  # gets a fresh allocation and the push cancels this stale run via the PR
  # concurrency group. NEVER `gh run rerun`: it reallocates into the same
  # degraded pool. One retrigger max per head commit (loop guard below).
  watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # empty-commit retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs only: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref.
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Detect a timeout-type failure
        id: trip
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          trip=false
          for id in $(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '.jobs[] | select(.conclusion=="failure") | .id'); do
            # A job-level timeout cancels the running step: the job is
            # 'failure' but its LAST step is 'cancelled'. A real test
            # failure ends with a failed step.

Run-to-run variance on a loaded ARM runner pushed it to 12.35s → red.

The failure: 12.347s vs 12s bound — 2.9% over. The primary guard (row-copy envelope) is the real scaling guard; wall clock is only an absolute budget guard. The comment even says "Wall clock only bounds the absolute budget — ratios flake on shared runners... so no ratio is asserted here."

The fix (surgical, CI root cause): make the wall-clock bound robust to loaded shared runners without losing its teeth against the quadratic shape:

If the per-test timeout is 30s or 6x multiplier, the quadratic shape would hit the TEST timeout anyway, failing loudly — good.

blocks.text:
# Issue #194 (point 4): per-step duration telemetry. The jobs API already
  # records started/completed per step — dump it as a summary table plus a
  # raw artifact instead of instrumenting every step by hand.
  step-timings:
    name: Per-step timing telemetry
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      actions: read
    steps:
      - name: Collect per-step durations
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The jobs endpoint intermittently answers 502 (live on the
          # gh-1086 rework head 81ed7186: a single 502 failed the whole
          # telemetry leg). Same 3-attempt pattern as build-mobile's
          # "Install Flutter dependencies" — transient API errors retry,
          # a real failure still reds the step loudly.
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" > /tmp/jobs.json; then
              break
            fi
            if [ "$attempt" = 3 ]; then
              echo "::error::gh api jobs fetch failed after 3 attempts — GitHub API is erroring (502-class)"
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "::warning::gh api jobs fetch failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
            sleep 10
          done
          python3 - <<'EOF' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          import datetime, json
          jobs = json.load(open('/tmp/jobs.json'))['jobs']
          print('## Per-step durations\n')
          print('| job | step | duration | conclusion |')
          print('|---|---|---|---|')
          for j in jobs:
              for s in j.get('steps', []):
                  if not (s.get('started_at') and s.get('completed_at')):
                      continue
                  t0 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['started_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  t1 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['completed_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  print(f"| {j['name']} | {s['name']} | {int((t1 - t0).total_seconds())}s | {s['conclusion']} |")
          EOF
          cp /tmp/jobs.json step-timings.json

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: step-timings
          path: step-timings.json
          retention-days: 14

  # Issue #194 (point 4): >2x-baseline watchdog. The timeout-minutes above
  # are ≈2x the healthy job durations observed on main (shards 3-5 min,
  # flutter-tests ~6 min + fa_ui shards ~5 min since issue #283). A timeout means this run landed on a degraded
  # runner allocation; the remedy is a fresh EMPTY-COMMIT push — a new run
  # gets a fresh allocation and the push cancels this stale run via the PR
  # concurrency group. NEVER `gh run rerun`: it reallocates into the same
  # degraded pool. One retrigger max per head commit (loop guard below).
  watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # empty-commit retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs only: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref.
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Detect a timeout-type failure
        id: trip
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          trip=false
          for id in $(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '.jobs[] | select(.conclusion=="failure") | .id'); do
            # A job-level timeout cancels the running step: the job is
            # 'failure' but its LAST step is 'cancelled'. A real test
            # failure ends with a failed step.

Now I understand the test fully:

- Test: `live-tail appends scale near-linearly, not quadratically (#1497)` at test/trajectory/trajectory_snapshot_builder_test.dart:989-1046ish.
- Primary guard: `snapshotRowCopies` — deterministic, passes.
- Secondary guard: absolute wall clock `expect(sw.elapsed, lessThan(const Duration(seconds: 12)))`. The comment says: "a loaded CI runner measured 8.82s for this same green path (~4x this box)" — so on CI this loop takes ~8.8s, and the bound is 12s. Run-to-run variance on a loaded ARM runner pushed it to 12.35s → red.

The failure: 12.347s vs 12s bound — 2.9% over. The primary guard (row-copy envelope) is the real scaling guard; wall clock is only an absolute budget guard. The comment even says "Wall clock only bounds the absolute budget — ratios flake on shared runners... so no ratio is asserted here."

The fix (surgical, CI root cause): make the wall-clock bound robust to loaded shared runners without losing its teeth against the quadratic shape:
- Quadratic shape measured 31s (pre-#1497) on a dev box; on a CI box ~4x slower that's ≥31s? Actually 31s was "the pre-#1497 shape measured 31s for the same loop" (on the M4 Pro dev box presumably). On CI ~4x → the quadratic would take ~2 minutes; and CI `dart test` has a 30s-per-test default timeout?? Hmm — actually dart_test.yaml may set timeouts. Let me check dart_test.yaml. If the per-test timeout is 30s or 6x multiplier, the quadratic shape would hit the TEST timeout anyway, failing loudly — good.

Options:
1. Raise the bound 12s → a value that absorbs CI variance but still catches quadratic (31s dev-box, ≥60s+ on CI): e.g. 20s. But the observed CI green-path time is 8.82s... and now 12.35s under load. The margin to quadratic (31s+ even on fast boxes) leaves room: 20s still fails nothing green (worst observed 12.35) and still splits from ≥31s quadratic. Hmm 20 < 31, ok but on a fast box quadratic is 31s — bound must stay below that. 20s gives 1.6x headroom over the worst observed CI green time.

But wait — is that the right fix, or should the wall-clock bound be made load-adaptive? Look at repo conventions: the sibling test "appendAll 50k records stays within the open budget" uses `lessThan(const Duration(seconds: 5))` for a single bulk appendAll — locally it'd run in well under a second; on CI ~4x slower + load, 5s could flake too... but it passed. The comment for the 12s bound explicitly documents prior flake-tuning ("12s (not 8s): a loaded CI runner measured 8.82s"). So the established pattern = absolute wall-clock budget tuned with documented margin. This test already flaked once at 8.82 → they set 12. Now it measured 12.35.

Given "red 1/3, 2/3, LAST CHANCE" — the stakes are high; a mere 12→20 bump risks another marginal red (if a loaded runner measures 2.5x of 8.8 ≈ 22s...). Options analysis:

Option A: Raise to 20s. Precedent comment documents the trade-off. Risk: another loaded run > 20s → third red → escalation.

Option B: Remove the wall-clock assertion entirely, keeping the deterministic `snapshotRowCopies` envelope (the primary guard) + the sibling 50k open-budget test's 5s absolute bound (which still bounds absolute cost of the same builder path). The comment says wall clock "only bounds the absolute budget" — the budget is ALSO bounded by the sibling test (`appendAll 50k ... within the open budget`, 5s for 12.5k bulk appends... though that's appendAll not live-tail loop).

Hmm. But the repo convention (issue #358 comment) is: "ratios flake on shared runners" → prefer deterministic operation counts; wall clock only as a coarse budget. They kept a coarse budget deliberately. A quadratic regression would still be caught by snapshotRowCopies (3 orders of magnitude) — the wall clock is a redundant secondary guard.

Option C: Tag-based skip on CI — no, tests must still guard.

Option D: Make the bound machine-calibrated: measure a tiny calibration loop first and scale. Over-engineering vs repo conventions.

The cleanest surgical fix that preserves both intent and robustness: raise the absolute budget to a value that (a) still fails the quadratic shape on ANY box (≥31s measured on a fast box — the bound must stay below that: choose 25s), and (b) absorbs the worst observed loaded-CI green time with real headroom (12.35s observed → 25s = 2x headroom). But if a pathological loaded runner does 4x the 8.8s (35s)... then green path exceeds 25s and we'd red again while quadratic on same box would be ~4x31=124s. Ugh — wall-clock bounds on shared runners can't be fully robust while keeping teeth.

Alternative sharper approach: keep absolute bound generous AND anchor the quadratic-distinction on the deterministic envelope (already present). I.e., wall clock becomes a true "insane budget" trip-wire: e.g. 30s < quadratic-on-fast-box(31s)... that's cutting too close to the quadratic on a fast box. Quadratic on fast box 31s → bound must be < 31s on fast box. On fast box, green path is ~1-3s (dev box "well under 100ms warmed; cold JIT cliff stays under 3s (M4 Pro)"). Hmm wait — on the dev box green is <3s, quadratic 31s → 10x gap. On CI (4x slower): green 8.8-12.4s, quadratic ~124s → still 10x gap. So a bound of 20s: on CI, green worst 12.4 → passes with 1.6x headroom; quadratic (124s CI / 31s dev) fails. On a fast box, 20s bound vs green <3s and quadratic 31s → marginally fails (31 > 20) ✓.

20s gives: worst observed green = 12.35s → 62% headroom. Quadratic fails on every box measured. Hmm, but 1.6x headroom — a 30s scheduler stall (GC pause, hypervisor steal) inside the loop could still flip it. The prior comment noted "one GC pause, scheduler deschedule, or hypervisor steal" as flip risks for ratios — same risk applies to absolute bounds. 

Better: split the difference — raise to 30s? On dev box quadratic = 31s — the bound would NOT fail the quadratic on a fast box. But would the quadratic even reach the assertion on a dev box? 31s loop — dart_test per-test timeout (dart_test.yaml). Let me check dart_test.yaml for timeout config. If per-test timeout is e.g. 6x/30s, the quadratic shape would time out the test (red) anyway on fast boxes, and on CI it'd be ~124s → definitely red via timeout. So a 30s wall bound would be redundant-but-harmless... but it weakens "the quadratic shape must fail THIS guard" documented intent.

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf

Repo convention (issue #358 lesson, written into this very file): wall clock cannot distinguish a slow machine from a quadratic algorithm; deterministic operation counting is the preferred guard; absolute open budgets (5s-style) are used for cheaper operations (single bulk appendAll) where margin is huge (sub-second → 5s = 5x+).

blocks.text:
# Issue #194 (point 4): per-step duration telemetry. The jobs API already
  # records started/completed per step — dump it as a summary table plus a
  # raw artifact instead of instrumenting every step by hand.
  step-timings:
    name: Per-step timing telemetry
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      actions: read
    steps:
      - name: Collect per-step durations
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The jobs endpoint intermittently answers 502 (live on the
          # gh-1086 rework head 81ed7186: a single 502 failed the whole
          # telemetry leg). Same 3-attempt pattern as build-mobile's
          # "Install Flutter dependencies" — transient API errors retry,
          # a real failure still reds the step loudly.
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" > /tmp/jobs.json; then
              break
            fi
            if [ "$attempt" = 3 ]; then
              echo "::error::gh api jobs fetch failed after 3 attempts — GitHub API is erroring (502-class)"
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "::warning::gh api jobs fetch failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
            sleep 10
          done
          python3 - <<'EOF' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          import datetime, json
          jobs = json.load(open('/tmp/jobs.json'))['jobs']
          print('## Per-step durations\n')
          print('| job | step | duration | conclusion |')
          print('|---|---|---|---|')
          for j in jobs:
              for s in j.get('steps', []):
                  if not (s.get('started_at') and s.get('completed_at')):
                      continue
                  t0 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['started_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  t1 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['completed_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  print(f"| {j['name']} | {s['name']} | {int((t1 - t0).total_seconds())}s | {s['conclusion']} |")
          EOF
          cp /tmp/jobs.json step-timings.json

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: step-timings
          path: step-timings.json
          retention-days: 14

  # Issue #194 (point 4): >2x-baseline watchdog. The timeout-minutes above
  # are ≈2x the healthy job durations observed on main (shards 3-5 min,
  # flutter-tests ~6 min + fa_ui shards ~5 min since issue #283). A timeout means this run landed on a degraded
  # runner allocation; the remedy is a fresh EMPTY-COMMIT push — a new run
  # gets a fresh allocation and the push cancels this stale run via the PR
  # concurrency group. NEVER `gh run rerun`: it reallocates into the same
  # degraded pool. One retrigger max per head commit (loop guard below).
  watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # empty-commit retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs only: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref.
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Detect a timeout-type failure
        id: trip
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          trip=false
          for id in $(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '.jobs[] | select(.conclusion=="failure") | .id'); do
            # A job-level timeout cancels the running step: the job is
            # 'failure' but its LAST step is 'cancelled'. A real test
            # failure ends with a failed step.

The cleanest surgical fix that preserves both intent and robustness: raise the absolute budget to a value that (a) still fails the quadratic shape on ANY box (≥31s measured on a fast box — the bound must stay below that: choose 25s), and (b) absorbs the worst observed loaded-CI green time with real headroom (12.35s observed → 25s = 2x headroom). Ugh — wall-clock bounds on shared runners can't be fully robust while keeping teeth.

Alternative sharper approach: keep absolute bound generous AND anchor the quadratic-distinction on the deterministic envelope (already present). I.e., wall clock becomes a true "insane budget" trip-wire: e.g. 30s < quadratic-on-fast-box(31s)... that's cutting too close to the quadratic on a fast box. 20s gives: worst observed green = 12.35s → 62% headroom. Quadratic fails on every box measured. Now, which is the right fix shape? Let me look at how OTHER tests in this exact file handle the wall-clock + they all have absolute budgets (5s ones passed on CI: "30k-record bulk load stays within the open budget" 5s, "appendAll 50k records stays within the open budget" 5s). The 12s one is for a 20k-append LIVE loop — the most expensive one.

Key data points:

- CI ARM runner: measured 8.82s (green path, loaded) — recorded earlier; now 12.35s → failed at 12s bound.

The 12.35s failure is +40% over the previously observed 8.82s. Runner load varies. To make this robust I could:

Option A: bump 12 → 20s (still < 31s quadratic on the FASTEST box; headroom 1.6x over worst observed).

Option B: drop the wall-clock line, rely on the deterministic snapshotRowCopies envelope (primary guard, 3 orders of magnitude separation) + the two sibling 5s absolute budgets that still bound the builder's absolute cost on other paths. The comment block itself says the row-copy envelope is "the primary guard regardless".

The test's PURPOSE is regression-guarding the #1497 quadratic. The wall-clock assertion's incremental value over the deterministic envelope is small; its flake cost is proven (this red, plus the #358 predecessor flaked twice leading to its replacement by an operation count).

Repo convention (issue #358 lesson, written into this very file): wall clock cannot distinguish a slow machine from a quadratic algorithm; deterministic operation counting is the preferred guard; absolute open budgets (5s-style) are used for cheaper operations (single bulk appendAll) where margin is huge (sub-second → 5s = 5x+).

Given the stakes (LAST CHANCE before human escalation, red 2/3), the most robust surgical fix preserving the guard intent:
1. Keep the deterministic snapshotRowCopies envelope (untouched — primary scaling guard).
2. Replace the knife-edge absolute bound with a form that keeps absolute-budget teeth but tolerates shared-runner noise: raise 12s → 20s AND... hmm, honestly 20s vs observed 12.35s is only 1.6x.

Actually — let me look at what measured 12.35s: "warmed runs do this in well under 100ms; even a cold JIT-tier cliff stays under 3s (M4 Pro)... a loaded CI runner measured 8.82s for this same green path (~4x this box)". CI is 4x the dev box. If CI load doubles again: 24s > 20s → red again. If I set 30s: on the dev box the quadratic measured 31s — barely above the bound; a future quadratic regression on a faster dev box could pass the wall-clock line... but it would still be caught by snapshotRowCopies (3 orders of magnitude, deterministic — the true guard). And the per-test timeout in CI... default dart test timeout is 30s per test! Wait — package:test default timeout is 30s per test unless overridden. This test loop measured 12.35s on CI; a quadratic at ≥31s on dev box / ≥120s on CI would hit the 30s per-test DEFAULT timeout → the test FAILS via timeout anyway!

Let me verify the default timeout isn't overridden in dart_test.yaml (no `timeout` key present — correct, the file above has only tags). So package:test default 30s per-test timeout applies. That means:
- Any wall-clock bound ≥30s is redundant: the framework's own timeout enforces 30s.
- The quadratic shape (31s+) already fails via per-test timeout on any box.

So raising the bound to 20s keeps the explicit assertion meaningful (< 20s fails before the framework's 30s timeout) and doubles headroom over the worst observed CI time (12.35s), while the deterministic row-copy envelope remains the scaling guard and the framework timeout remains the absolute backstop. Hmm — but is 20s enough headroom? Worst observed: 12.35 (this run), 8.82 (earlier). 20/12.35 = 1.62x. A hypothetical heavier-loaded runner: shard runs 182 files with default concurrency (CI runner = 4 cores? ubuntu-24.04-arm... package:test default concurrency = CPU count). The trajectory test runs while OTHER tests run concurrently — that's why CI is 4x slower than dev box.

Alternative stronger shape: align with the sibling "open budget" tests (5s) — no. The live-tail loop is 20k appends; on CI it costs ~9-12s; can't get it under 5s.

What about reducing the work? E.g. halve the fixture to 2500 turns (10k records)? That changes what the test measures — the #1497 incident was at 65k live appends; 20k is already a scaled-down proxy. Halving again weakens the regression signal... but the PRIMARY guard (row copies per append) is size-independent: the quadratic fails the envelope at ANY n ≥ ~2x chunk size. The wall clock at 20k exists only as an "insane budget" trip-wire. Halving to 10k records: quadratic cost = n² — at 10k it'd still be ~31s*(10/20)²? No wait — quadratic 31s was measured at THIS size (20k appends). At 10k it'd be ~7.75s on dev box, ~31s on CI → the framework timeout (30s) would just barely catch it on CI but NOT on a dev box run (7.75s passes). So halving weakens the quadratic backstop on dev boxes. Keep 20k.

Decision: bump 12s → 20s with a comment documenting the third data point (12.35s red on the loaded ARM runner). This is the same remedy the test itself documents from its previous flake ("12s (not 8s): a loaded CI runner measured 8.82s"). It's the established iteration pattern for this exact assertion. The deterministic envelope + framework 30s timeout remain as stronger backstops.

Hmm — wait. Let me reconsider Option B (remove wall-clock entirely) once more. Arguments FOR removal: the file's own history shows wall-clock bounds in this file flaked repeatedly (#358 twice, #1497 once now); the deterministic counter is the primary guard; the 30s framework timeout bounds the absolute; two sibling 5s budgets bound bulk paths. The repo's pattern for this exact assertion's previous flake was: raise the budget + document the measurement. I'll follow it: 12 → 20s, and document the 12.35s CI data point.

Per TDD rules: "NEVER change production code in response to a review comment or CI failure without a test that first reproduces it". Here the failing thing IS a test (a too-tight test budget, not a production bug). The RED state = the test itself failed on CI. There's no production code change — I'm adjusting the test's environment-sensitivity. The "reproduction" is the CI log evidence: 12.347s vs 12s. A local re-run of the test passes (proving machine-dependence — exactly the #358-documented phenomenon: "Wall clock cannot tell 'slower machine' from 'quadratic algorithm'").

blocks.text:
# Issue #194 (point 4): per-step duration telemetry. The jobs API already
  # records started/completed per step — dump it as a summary table plus a
  # raw artifact instead of instrumenting every step by hand.
  step-timings:
    name: Per-step timing telemetry
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      actions: read
    steps:
      - name: Collect per-step durations
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The jobs endpoint intermittently answers 502 (live on the
          # gh-1086 rework head 81ed7186: a single 502 failed the whole
          # telemetry leg). Same 3-attempt pattern as build-mobile's
          # "Install Flutter dependencies" — transient API errors retry,
          # a real failure still reds the step loudly.
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" > /tmp/jobs.json; then
              break
            fi
            if [ "$attempt" = 3 ]; then
              echo "::error::gh api jobs fetch failed after 3 attempts — GitHub API is erroring (502-class)"
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "::warning::gh api jobs fetch failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
            sleep 10
          done
          python3 - <<'EOF' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          import datetime, json
          jobs = json.load(open('/tmp/jobs.json'))['jobs']
          print('## Per-step durations\n')
          print('| job | step | duration | conclusion |')
          print('|---|---|---|---|')
          for j in jobs:
              for s in j.get('steps', []):
                  if not (s.get('started_at') and s.get('completed_at')):
                      continue
                  t0 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['started_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  t1 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['completed_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  print(f"| {j['name']} | {s['name']} | {int((t1 - t0).total_seconds())}s | {s['conclusion']} |")
          EOF
          cp /tmp/jobs.json step-timings.json

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: step-timings
          path: step-timings.json
          retention-days: 14

  # Issue #194 (point 4): >2x-baseline watchdog. The timeout-minutes above
  # are ≈2x the healthy job durations observed on main (shards 3-5 min,
  # flutter-tests ~6 min + fa_ui shards ~5 min since issue #283). A timeout means this run landed on a degraded
  # runner allocation; the remedy is a fresh EMPTY-COMMIT push — a new run
  # gets a fresh allocation and the push cancels this stale run via the PR
  # concurrency group. NEVER `gh run rerun`: it reallocates into the same
  # degraded pool. One retrigger max per head commit (loop guard below).
  watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # empty-commit retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs only: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,

      contents: write

      - name: Detect a timeout-type failure
        id: trip
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          trip=false
          for id in $(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '.jobs[] | select(.conclusion=="failure") | .id'); do
            # A job-level timeout cancels the running step: the job is
            # 'failure' but its LAST step is 'cancelled'. A real test

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only

    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:

  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic

blocks.text:
# Issue #194 (point 4): per-step duration telemetry. The jobs API already
  # records started/completed per step — dump it as a summary table plus a
  # raw artifact instead of instrumenting every step by hand.
  step-timings:
    name: Per-step timing telemetry
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      actions: read
    steps:
      - name: Collect per-step durations
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The jobs endpoint intermittently answers 502 (live on the
          # gh-1086 rework head 81ed7186: a single 502 failed the whole
          # telemetry leg). Same 3-attempt pattern as build-mobile's
          # "Install Flutter dependencies" — transient API errors retry,
          # a real failure still reds the step loudly.
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" > /tmp/jobs.json; then
              break
            fi
            if [ "$attempt" = 3 ]; then
              echo "::error::gh api jobs fetch failed after 3 attempts — GitHub API is erroring (502-class)"
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "::warning::gh api jobs fetch failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
            sleep 10
          done
          python3 - <<'EOF' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          import datetime, json
          jobs = json.load(open('/tmp/jobs.json'))['jobs']
          print('## Per-step durations\n')
          print('| job | step | duration | conclusion |')
          print('|---|---|---|---|')
          for j in jobs:
              for s in j.get('steps', []):
                  if not (s.get('started_at') and s.get('completed_at')):
                      continue
                  t0 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['started_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  t1 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['completed_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  print(f"| {j['name']} | {s['name']} | {int((t1 - t0).total_seconds())}s | {s['conclusion']} |")
          EOF
          cp /tmp/jobs.json step-timings.json

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: step-timings
          path: step-timings.json
          retention-days: 14

  # Issue #194 (point 4): >2x-baseline watchdog. The timeout-minutes above
  # are ≈2x the healthy job durations observed on main (shards 3-5 min,
  # flutter-tests ~6 min + fa_ui shards ~5 min since issue #283). A timeout means this run landed on a degraded
  # runner allocation; the remedy is a fresh EMPTY-COMMIT push — a new run
  # gets a fresh allocation and the push cancels this stale run via the PR
  # concurrency group. NEVER `gh run rerun`: it reallocates into the same
  # degraded pool. One retrigger max per head commit (loop guard below).
  watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # empty-commit retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs only: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref.
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Detect a timeout-type failure
        id: trip
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          trip=false
          for id in $(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '.jobs[] | select(.conclusion=="failure") | .id'); do
            # A job-level timeout cancels the running step: the job is
            # 'failure' but its LAST step is 'cancelled'. A real test

# Issue #194 (point 4): per-step duration telemetry. The jobs API already
  # records started/completed per step — dump it as a summary table plus a

blocks.text:
# Issue #194 (point 4): per-step duration telemetry. The jobs API already
  # records started/completed per step — dump it as a summary table plus a
  # raw artifact instead of instrumenting every step by hand.
  step-timings:
    name: Per-step timing telemetry
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      actions: read
    steps:
      - name: Collect per-step durations
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The jobs endpoint intermittently answers 502 (live on the
          # gh-1086 rework head 81ed7186: a single 502 failed the whole
          # telemetry leg). Same 3-attempt pattern as build-mobile's
          # "Install Flutter dependencies" — transient API errors retry,
          # a real failure still reds the step loudly.
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" > /tmp/jobs.json; then
              break
            fi
            if [ "$attempt" = 3 ]; then
              echo "::error::gh api jobs fetch failed after 3 attempts — GitHub API is erroring (502-class)"
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "::warning::gh api jobs fetch failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
            sleep 10
          done
          python3 - <<'EOF' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          import datetime, json
          jobs = json.load(open('/tmp/jobs.json'))['jobs']
          print('## Per-step durations\n')
          print('| job | step | duration | conclusion |')
          print('|---|---|---|---|')
          for j in jobs:
              for s in j.get('steps', []):
                  if not (s.get('started_at') and s.get('completed_at')):
                      continue
                  t0 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['started_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  t1 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['completed_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  print(f"| {j['name']} | {s['name']} | {int((t1 - t0).total_seconds())}s | {s['conclusion']} |")
          EOF
          cp /tmp/jobs.json step-timings.json

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: step-timings
          path: step-timings.json
          retention-days: 14

  # Issue #194 (point 4): >2x-baseline watchdog. The timeout-minutes above
  # are ≈2x the healthy job durations observed on main (shards 3-5 min,
  # flutter-tests ~6 min + fa_ui shards ~5 min since issue #283). A timeout means this run landed on a degraded
  # runner allocation; the remedy is a fresh EMPTY-COMMIT push — a new run
  # gets a fresh allocation and the push cancels this stale run via the PR
  # concurrency group. NEVER `gh run rerun`: it reallocates into the same
  # degraded pool. One retrigger max per head commit (loop guard below).
  watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # empty-commit retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs only: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref.
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Detect a timeout-type failure
        id: trip
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          trip=false
          for id in $(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '.jobs[] | select(.conclusion=="failure") | .id'); do
            # A job-level timeout cancels the running step: the job is
            # 'failure' but its LAST step is 'cancelled'. A real test
            # failure ends with a failed step.

Now I understand the test fully:

- Test: `live-tail appends scale near-linearly, not quadratically (#1497)` at test/trajectory/trajectory_snapshot_builder_test.dart:989-1046ish.
- Primary guard: `snapshotRowCopies` — deterministic, passes.
- Secondary guard: absolute wall clock `expect(sw.elapsed, lessThan(const Duration(seconds: 12)))`. The comment says: "a loaded CI runner measured 8.82s for this same green path (~4x this box)" — so on CI this loop takes ~8.8s, and the bound is 12s. Run-to-run variance on a loaded ARM runner pushed it to 12.35s → red.

The failure: 12.347s vs 12s bound — 2.9% over. The primary guard (row-copy envelope) is the real scaling guard; wall clock is only an absolute budget guard. The comment even says "Wall clock only bounds the absolute budget — ratios flake on shared runners... so no ratio is asserted here."

The fix (surgical, CI root cause): make the wall-clock bound robust to loaded shared runners without losing its teeth against the quadratic shape:
- Quadratic shape measured 31s (pre-#1497) on a dev box; on a CI box ~4x slower that's ≥31s? Actually 31s was "the pre-#1497 shape measured 31s for the same loop" (on the M4 Pro dev box presumably). On CI ~4x → the quadratic would take ~2 minutes; and CI `dart test` has a 30s-per-test default timeout?? Hmm — actually dart_test.yaml may set timeouts. Let me check dart_test.yaml. If the per-test timeout is 30s or 6x multiplier, the quadratic shape would hit the TEST timeout anyway, failing loudly — good.

Options:
1. Raise the bound 12s → a value that absorbs CI variance but still catches quadratic (31s dev-box, ≥60s+ on CI): e.g. 20s. But the observed CI green-path time is 8.82s... and now 12.35s under load. The margin to quadratic (31s+ even on fast boxes) leaves room: 20s still fails nothing green (worst observed 12.35) and still splits from ≥31s quadratic. Hmm 20 < 31, ok but on a fast box quadratic is 31s — bound must stay below that. 20s gives 1.6x headroom over the worst observed CI green time.

But wait — is that the right fix, or should the wall-clock bound be made load-adaptive? Look at repo conventions: the sibling test "appendAll 50k records stays within the open budget" uses `lessThan(const Duration(seconds: 5))` for a single bulk appendAll — locally it'd run in well under a second; on CI ~4x slower + load, 5s could flake too... but it passed. The comment for the 12s bound explicitly documents prior flake-tuning ("12s (not 8s): a loaded CI runner measured 8.82s"). So the established pattern = absolute wall-clock budget tuned with documented margin. This test already flaked once at 8.82 → they set 12. Now it measured 12.35.

Given "red 1/3, 2/3, LAST CHANCE" — the stakes are high; a mere 12→20 bump risks another marginal red (if a loaded runner measures 2.5x of 8.8 ≈ 22s...). Options analysis:

Option A: Raise to 20s. Precedent comment documents the trade-off. Risk: another loaded run > 20s → third red → escalation.

Option B: Remove the wall-clock assertion entirely, keeping the deterministic `snapshotRowCopies` envelope (the primary guard) + the sibling 50k open-budget test's 5s absolute bound (which still bounds absolute cost of the same builder path). The comment says wall clock "only bounds the absolute budget" — the budget is ALSO bounded by the sibling test (`appendAll 50k ... within the open budget`, 5s for 12.5k bulk appends... though that's appendAll not live-tail loop).

Hmm. But the repo convention (issue #358 comment) is: "ratios flake on shared runners" → prefer deterministic operation counts; wall clock only as a coarse budget. They kept a coarse budget deliberately. A quadratic regression would still be caught by snapshotRowCopies (3 orders of magnitude) — the wall clock is a redundant secondary guard.

Option C: Tag-based skip on CI — no, tests must still guard.

Option D: Make the bound machine-calibrated: measure a tiny calibration loop first and scale. Over-engineering vs repo conventions.

The cleanest surgical fix that preserves both intent and robustness: raise the absolute budget to a value that (a) still fails the quadratic shape on ANY box (≥31s measured on a fast box — the bound must stay below that: choose 25s), and (b) absorbs the worst observed loaded-CI green time with real headroom (12.35s observed → 25s = 2x headroom). But if a pathological loaded runner does 4x the 8.8s (35s)... then green path exceeds 25s and we'd red again while quadratic on same box would be ~4x31=124s. blocks.text:
# Issue #194 (point 4): per-step duration telemetry. The jobs API already
  # records started/completed per step — dump it as a summary table plus a
  # raw artifact instead of instrumenting every step by hand.
  step-timings:
    name: Per-step timing telemetry
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      actions: read
    steps:
      - name: Collect per-step durations
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The jobs endpoint intermittently answers 502 (live on the
          # gh-1086 rework head 81ed7186: a single 502 failed the whole
          # telemetry leg). Same 3-attempt pattern as build-mobile's
          # "Install Flutter dependencies" — transient API errors retry,
          # a real failure still reds the step loudly.
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" > /tmp/jobs.json; then
              break
            fi
            if [ "$attempt" = 3 ]; then
              echo "::error::gh api jobs fetch failed after 3 attempts — GitHub API is erroring (502-class)"
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "::warning::gh api jobs fetch failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
            sleep 10
          done
          python3 - <<'EOF' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          import datetime, json
          jobs = json.load(open('/tmp/jobs.json'))['jobs']
          print('## Per-step durations\n')
          print('| job | step | duration | conclusion |')
          print('|---|---|---|---|')
          for j in jobs:
              for s in j.get('steps', []):
                  if not (s.get('started_at') and s.get('completed_at')):
                      continue
                  t0 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['started_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  t1 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['completed_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  print(f"| {j['name']} | {s['name']} | {int((t1 - t0).total_seconds())}s | {s['conclusion']} |")
          EOF
          cp /tmp/jobs.json step-timings.json

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: step-timings
          path: step-timings.json
          retention-days: 14

  # Issue #194 (point 4): >2x-baseline watchdog. The timeout-minutes above
  # are ≈2x the healthy job durations observed on main (shards 3-5 min,
  # flutter-tests ~6 min + fa_ui shards ~5 min since issue #283). A timeout means this run landed on a degraded
  # runner allocation; the remedy is a fresh EMPTY-COMMIT push — a new run
  # gets a fresh allocation and the push cancels this stale run via the PR
  # concurrency group. NEVER `gh run rerun`: it reallocates into the same
  # degraded pool. One retrigger max per head commit (loop guard below).
  watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # empty-commit retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs only: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref.
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Detect a timeout-type failure
        id: trip
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          trip=false
          for id in $(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '.jobs[] | select(.conclusion=="failure") | .id'); do
            # A job-level timeout cancels the running step: the job is
            # 'failure' but its LAST step is 'cancelled'. A real test
            # failure ends with a failed step.

Now I understand the test fully:

- Test: `live-tail appends scale near-linearly, not quadratically (#1497)` at test/trajectory/trajectory_snapshot_builder_test.dart:989-1046ish.
- Primary guard: `snapshotRowCopies` — deterministic, passes.
- Secondary guard: absolute wall clock `expect(sw.elapsed, lessThan(const Duration(seconds: 12)))`. The comment says: "a loaded CI runner measured 8.82s for this same green path (~4x this box)" — so on CI this loop takes ~8.8s, and the bound is 12s. Run-to-run variance on a loaded ARM runner pushed it to 12.35s → red.

The failure: 12.347s vs 12s bound — 2.9% over. The primary guard (row-copy envelope) is the real scaling guard; wall clock is only an absolute budget guard. The comment even says "Wall clock only bounds the absolute budget — ratios flake on shared runners... so no ratio is asserted here."

The fix (surgical, CI root cause): make the wall-clock bound robust to loaded shared runners without losing its teeth against the quadratic shape:
- Quadratic shape measured 31s (pre-#1497) on a dev box; on a CI box ~4x slower that's ≥31s? Actually 31s was "the pre-#1497 shape measured 31s for the same loop" (on the M4 Pro dev box presumably). On CI ~4x → the quadratic would take ~2 minutes; and CI `dart test` has a 30s-per-test default timeout?? Hmm — actually dart_test.yaml may set timeouts. Let me check dart_test.yaml. If the per-test timeout is 30s or 6x multiplier, the quadratic shape would hit the TEST timeout anyway, failing loudly — good.

Options:
1. Raise the bound 12s → a value that absorbs CI variance but still catches quadratic (31s dev-box, ≥60s+ on CI): e.g. 20s. But the observed CI green-path time is 8.82s... and now 12.35s under load. The margin to quadratic (31s+ even on fast boxes) leaves room: 20s still fails nothing green (worst observed 12.35) and still splits from ≥31s quadratic. Hmm 20 < 31, ok but on a fast box quadratic is 31s — bound must stay below that. 20s gives 1.6x headroom over the worst observed CI green time.

But wait — is that the right fix, or should the wall-clock bound be made load-adaptive? Look at repo conventions: the sibling test "appendAll 50k records stays within the open budget" uses `lessThan(const Duration(seconds: 5))` for a single bulk appendAll — locally it'd run in well under a second; on CI ~4x slower + load, 5s could flake too... but it passed. The comment for the 12s bound explicitly documents prior flake-tuning ("12s (not 8s): a loaded CI runner measured 8.82s"). So the established pattern = absolute wall-clock budget tuned with documented margin. This test already flaked once at 8.82 → they set 12. Now it measured 12.35.

Given "red 1/3, 2/3, LAST CHANCE" — the stakes are high; a mere 12→20 bump risks another marginal red (if a loaded runner measures 2.5x of 8.8 ≈ 22s...). Options analysis:

Option A: Raise to 20s. Precedent comment documents the trade-off. Risk: another loaded run > 20s → third red → escalation.

Option B: Remove the wall-clock assertion entirely, keeping the deterministic `snapshotRowCopies` envelope (the primary guard) + the sibling 50k open-budget test's 5s absolute bound (which still bounds absolute cost of the same builder path). The comment says wall clock "only bounds the absolute budget" — the budget is ALSO bounded by the sibling test (`appendAll 50k ... within the open budget`, 5s for 12.5k bulk appends... though that's appendAll not live-tail loop).

Hmm. But the repo convention (issue #358 comment) is: "ratios flake on shared runners" → prefer deterministic operation counts; wall clock only as a coarse budget. They kept a coarse budget deliberately. A quadratic regression would still be caught by snapshotRowCopies (3 orders of magnitude) — the wall clock is a redundant secondary guard.

Option C: Tag-based skip on CI — no, tests must still guard.

Option D: Make the bound machine-calibrated: measure a tiny calibration loop first and scale. Over-engineering vs repo conventions.

The cleanest surgical fix that preserves both intent and robustness: raise the absolute budget to a value that (a) still fails the quadratic shape on ANY box (≥31s measured on a fast box — the bound must stay below that: choose 25s), and (b) absorbs the worst observed loaded-CI green time with real headroom (12.35s observed → 25s = 2x headroom). But if a pathological loaded runner does 4x the 8.8s (35s)... then green path exceeds 25s and we'd red again while quadratic on same box would be ~4x31=124s. Ugh — wall-clock bounds on shared runners can't be fully robust while keeping teeth.

Alternative sharper approach: keep absolute bound generous AND anchor the quadratic-distinction on the deterministic envelope (already present). I.e., wall clock becomes a true "insane budget" trip-wire: e.g. 30s < quadratic-on-fast-box(31s)... that's cutting too close to the quadratic on a fast box. Quadratic on fast box 31s → bound must be < 31s on fast box. On fast box, green path is ~1-3s (dev box "well under 100ms warmed; cold JIT cliff stays under 3s (M4 Pro)"). Hmm wait — on the dev box green is <3s, quadratic 31s → 10x gap. On CI (4x slower): green 8.8-12.4s, quadratic ~124s → still 10x gap. So a bound of 20s: on CI, green worst 12.4 → passes with 1.6x headroom; quadratic (124s CI / 31s dev) fails. On a fast box, 20s bound vs green <3s and quadratic 31s → marginally fails (31 > 20) ✓.

20s gives: worst observed green = 12.35s → 62% headroom. Quadratic fails on every box measured. Hmm, but 1.6x headroom — a 30s scheduler stall (GC pause, hypervisor steal) inside the loop could still flip it. The prior comment noted "one GC pause, scheduler deschedule, or hypervisor steal" as flip risks for ratios — same risk applies to absolute bounds. 

Better: split the difference — raise to 30s? On dev box quadratic = 31s — the bound would NOT fail the quadratic on a fast box. But would the quadratic even reach the assertion on a dev box? 31s loop — dart_test per-test timeout (dart_test.yaml). Let me check dart_test.yaml for timeout config.   browser-ext:

    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need

    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a

    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty

    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open

Repo convention (issue #358 lesson, written into this very file): wall clock cannot distinguish a slow machine from a quadratic algorithm; deterministic operation counting is the preferred guard; absolute open budgets (5s-style) are used for cheaper operations (single bulk appendAll) where margin is huge (sub-second → 5s = 5x+).

This test loop measured 12.35s on CI; a quadratic at ≥31s on dev box / ≥120s on CI would hit the 30s per-test DEFAULT timeout → the test FAILS via timeout anyway!

Let me verify the default timeout isn't overridden in dart_test.yaml (no `timeout` key present — correct, the file above has only tags). So package:test default 30s per-test timeout applies. That means:
- Any wall-clock bound ≥30s is redundant: the framework's own timeout enforces 30s.

So raising the bound to 20s keeps the explicit assertion meaningful (< 20s fails before the framework's 30s timeout) and doubles headroom over the worst observed CI time (12.35s), while the deterministic row-copy envelope remains the scaling guard and the framework timeout remains the absolute backstop. Hmm — but is 20s enough headroom? Worst observed: 12.35 (this run), 8.82 (earlier). 20/12.35 = 1.62x. blocks.text:
# Issue #194 (point 4): per-step duration telemetry. The jobs API already
  # records started/completed per step — dump it as a summary table plus a
  # raw artifact instead of instrumenting every step by hand.
  step-timings:
    name: Per-step timing telemetry
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      actions: read
    steps:
      - name: Collect per-step durations
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The jobs endpoint intermittently answers 502 (live on the
          # gh-1086 rework head 81ed7186: a single 502 failed the whole
          # telemetry leg). Same 3-attempt pattern as build-mobile's
          # "Install Flutter dependencies" — transient API errors retry,
          # a real failure still reds the step loudly.
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" > /tmp/jobs.json; then
              break
            fi
            if [ "$attempt" = 3 ]; then
              echo "::error::gh api jobs fetch failed after 3 attempts — GitHub API is erroring (502-class)"
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "::warning::gh api jobs fetch failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
            sleep 10
          done
          python3 - <<'EOF' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          import datetime, json
          jobs = json.load(open('/tmp/jobs.json'))['jobs']
          print('## Per-step durations\n')
          print('| job | step | duration | conclusion |')
          print('|---|---|---|---|')
          for j in jobs:
              for s in j.get('steps', []):
                  if not (s.get('started_at') and s.get('completed_at')):
                      continue
                  t0 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['started_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  t1 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['completed_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  print(f"| {j['name']} | {s['name']} | {int((t1 - t0).total_seconds())}s | {s['conclusion']} |")
          EOF
          cp /tmp/jobs.json step-timings.json

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: step-timings
          path: step-timings.json
          retention-days: 14

  # Issue #194 (point 4): >2x-baseline watchdog. The timeout-minutes above
  # are ≈2x the healthy job durations observed on main (shards 3-5 min,
  # flutter-tests ~6 min + fa_ui shards ~5 min since issue #283). A timeout means this run landed on a degraded
  # runner allocation; the remedy is a fresh EMPTY-COMMIT push — a new run
  # gets a fresh allocation and the push cancels this stale run via the PR
  # concurrency group. NEVER `gh run rerun`: it reallocates into the same
  # degraded pool. One retrigger max per head commit (loop guard below).
  watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # empty-commit retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs only: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref.
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Detect a timeout-type failure
        id: trip
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          trip=false
          for id in $(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '.jobs[] | select(.conclusion=="failure") | .id'); do
            # A job-level timeout cancels the running step: the job is
            # 'failure' but its LAST step is 'cancelled'. A real test
            # failure ends with a failed step.

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test

    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart
